newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse shrugs off minister dismissal.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse shrugs off minister dismissal.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange on Monday shrugged off Industry and Trade minister Tamas Suchman's dismissal as the BUX index soared to a second successive high.
The BUX index ended at 3,634.80, up 26.79 points.
BUX index futures advanced by between five and 20 points for five maturities and closed unchanged for the longest, 1998 June termin, at 4,660.00 points.
"His (Suchman's) dismissal left the market intact," said Adam Santha of Daiwa-MKB Rt.
"I don't think his removal shook investors' confidence too much," added Peter Lencs of MKB Securities.

Prime Minister Gyula Horn's office said on Sunday that Suchman, who was also in charge of the state privatisation agency APV Rt, would be dismissed from October 15. The announcement followed a scandal involving illegal payments by APV amounting to millions of dollars to a consultant.
In addition, defying earlier expectations for limited turnover due to investors' cautiosness, the daily turnover amounted to 1.49 billion forints.
"OTP, oil company MOL and chemical company TVK all had quite good turnover," Santha said.
OTP Bank led the rise of leading issues by leaping over five percent or 135 forints to end at 2,770.
TVK advanced 10 forints to close at 1,385 forints, remaining below the daily high of 1,415. MOL put on five forints to end at 1,620, up five, but closing below the daily peak of 1,630.
